the GaAs-like longitudinal optical (LO) phonons in GaAs1−XNx layers are affected by hydrogenation and strain, and that a linear relation should not be used to estimate strain from the frequency of the LO mode.

the GaAs-like longitudinal optical (LO) phonons of hydrogenated GaAsN layers are affected by the strain induced by hydrogen incorporation, which is different in different polarization configurations, and that the strain induced in GaAsN by hydrogen incorporation can be estimated by the frequency of the LO mode.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the influence of the strain on the GaAs-like phonon modes of GaAs1− xNx layers with low nitrogen concentrations, hydrogenated by different doses.

the study of the influence of hydrogen passivation on the Raman spectra of epitaxial layers of GaAs1− xNx (x < 0.02), with the aim of understanding the mechanisms of the observed relaxation of the GaAS-like LO phonon selection rules.

the development and application of a novel, non-destructive, optical technique, which can be applied in situ, to study the properties of hydrogenated GaAsN layers, with the aim of providing a deeper understanding of the hydrogen passivation mechanism.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the GaAs-like phonon mode selection rules in GaAs1−××××N layers can be relaxed in a way that depends on the H dose and on the light polarization.
the strain-related relaxation of the Gaas selection rules in hydrogen-ated GaAs1-xNx layers is a very complex phenomenon.
hydrogenation does not relax the GaAs-like selection rules but rather that the biaxially strained layers do.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the strain induced in the GaAs-like layers by the hydrogen passivation process can be relaxed by the application of an external stress, and that the hydrogen passivation of N-related acceptor levels in GaAs1− xNx can be achieved with a lower dose than that required in the case of GaAs.
the GaAs-like phonon mode selection rules can be relaxed by hydrogen passivation of GaAs1−XNx layers, but the evolution of the LO frequency with increasing H dose depends on the light polarization.
the strain induced by hydrogenation is a key factor in determining the evolution of the GaAs LO phonon frequency.
The main takeaway from our work is that
hydrogenation of GaAs1−XNx layers leads to a strain-induced relaxation of the GaN-like and the GaAs-like phonons selection rules, with a consequent increase of their frequency.

the strain related relaxation of the selection rules of the GaAs Raman modes can be exploited to determine the strain affecting the hydrogenated GaAsN layers, thus allowing to assess the H dose and the strain state of the structures.

hydrogen passivation of GaAsNx alloys can be achieved without inducing significant structural damage, as evidenced by the absence of Raman peaks associated to the formation of hydrogenated GaAsN clusters, and without affecting the GaAs-like phonon selection rules, which are relaxed due to biaxial stress induced by the hydrogenation process.
